name: Autosomal Dominant Diffuse Mutilating Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse, thickened hyperkeratosis on palms and soles
Progressive mutilation and spontaneous amputation of distal digits
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia with hyperkeratosis and parakeratosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diffuse palmoplantar hyperkeratosis with mutilating digital changes plus autosomal dominant inheritance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but no specific gene identified universally.

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperplasia, hyperkeratosis, and parakeratosis
imaging: X-rays showing resorption of distal phalanges
MRI may show soft tissue changes in digits
genetic: Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern observed in families
No single causative gene universally identified
other: Clinical observation of progressive mutilating palmoplantar keratoderma

distinguishingFeatures: Transgressive keratoderma extending beyond palms and soles

redFlags: Severe functional impairment of hands and feet
